newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bank 24 on target with 80,000 customers.
newsitem.headline: Bank 24 on target with 80,000 customers.

text.p: Bank 24, the telephone banking subsidiary of Deutsche Bank AG, said on Tuesday it would expand its customer base to 80,000 people by the end of the year as planned, and aimed to acquire a further 100,000 next year.
The introduction of banking via the Internet last October contributed to a strong inflow of customers in recent months, Bank 24 said in a statement.
More than 60 percent of Bank 24 customers come from savings banks and cooperative banks while 10 percent come from the parent bank, Bank 24 said.
The bank was set up in September 1995 as part of a drive by German banks to win customers through branchless banking and discount brokerage via telephone, fax and PC.
Bank 24 has said it aims to break even by 1999 and be the leader in the German direct banking market.
